name: open the pull request and post the plan on it
about: Push the branch and open the PR. Write the description first: what changed, why, and what has already been tested — it is the first thing every reader meets, and a PR without one costs each of them the same reconstruction. Then comment the plan onto it, with this step's `command` as it stands — that ONE plan and never the store, posted as the markdown it gives you, no fenced block, no summarising, no reformatting. It renders the plan AS IT STANDS AT THAT MOMENT — open steps, empty `output` fields and all — and waits for nothing: no step has to be finished first, and `merge` re-runs this same command later and edits the comment in place. So a definition telling you that some field of its own is what this comment dumps is saying why that field must be filled, never that the comment waits for it. The command is on the step so nobody has to reconstruct it; fill in the PR number and the plan id and run it. The whole record is the point: anyone reading the PR gets the state the lead has, rendered so they can actually read it. Nobody is asked whether to do any of this. Obliges `change-approval`, which obliges `review`, so naming this step lands THREE steps in one act — and each of them lands where it runs rather than where it was named: change approval is an early root of the plan and comes before the implementation, review comes after the implementation, and this step waits on the review. Nothing about those deps needs fixing afterwards, provided the implementation is already in the plan when you name this: a step is placed against the plan as it stands, and nothing already in it is re-deped.
